name_en: Sakana-zushi — whole mackerel or horse mackerel cured in vinegar over hand-shaped rice
summary_ja: サバやアジを背開きにして塩でしめ、酢に漬け込んでからすし飯にのせる宮崎沿岸部の姿ずし。天領地だった門川町の名物として知られ、四国から伝わったとの説もある冬祭りのごちそう。
summary_en: Mackerel or horse mackerel is butterflied, salted, then cured in vinegar before being set over hand-shaped rice — a whole-fish sushi from the Miyazaki coast, best known in Kadogawa, a former shogunate domain, and said by some to have crossed over from Shikoku; a winter-festival treat.
source_title: 魚ずし 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Nanatoko-zushi — a rice porridge of seven greens, gathered from seven neighboring homes
summary_ja: 大根や人参、せりなど七草と丸もちを煮込んだ雑炊を、近所の7軒からもらい集めて食べる旧島津藩都城地方の行事食。数え7歳の子どもが晴れ着で7軒を回る「ななとこさんの日」に食べられ、いまも神社での七草参りに名残が伝わる。
summary_en: A porridge of seven greens — daikon, carrot, water dropwort among them — and round mochi, gathered one bowl at a time from seven neighboring houses, eaten in the old Miyakonojo domain of the Shimazu clan. A seven-year-old child, dressed for the occasion, once made the rounds on Nanatoko-san no Hi; the custom lives on in a shrine visit for seven herbs.
source_title: 七とこずし 宮崎県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
